accessory bundles explained player-count bundles are the standing sets; signature bundles are 35% off but only with a table. the player number means accessories, not seating. # accessory bundles explained

two different things get called bundles, and they work differently.

## player-count accessory bundles

standing products you can buy any time, sized by how many players you're kitting out:

| bundle | price |
|---|---|
| pangea accessory bundle (2 players) | $109.99 |
| pangea accessory bundle (4 players) | $169.99 |

there are also focused ones — the **drink adapter bundle** ($55.98) pairs the mug and wine-glass adapters, and the **player desk bundle (4 players)** ($509.95) is four desks plus the 4-up stand.

there are also **utility series accessory bundles** — the hard-wearing café-grade line — in 2- and 4-player versions.

## signature bundles — 35% off, table purchase only

these are the curated sets at a real discount, and they're **only available alongside a table purchase**. they appear as an option while you're buying a table rather than as products you can find later.

that's worth knowing before you check out: if you dismiss the option and decide later you wanted it, the 35% isn't available on its own. see [signature bundles](signature-bundles.md).

## the player number means accessories, not seating

**"(6 players)" describes how many players' worth of accessories are in the box.** it is not a statement about how many people the table seats.

a 4-player bundle on a 4×6 that seats 8–10 is a perfectly normal purchase — you're kitting out four positions, not four seats. seating comes from the table: 3×3 seats 4, 3×5 seats 6, 4×6 seats 8–10.

## working out whether a bundle saves you money

bundles are priced below the same items bought individually, but the right question is whether you'd buy all of them. a bundle containing two things you want and three you don't isn't a saving.

the prices in [which accessories fit my table?](which-accessories-fit-my-table.md) let you add up the pieces you'd actually choose and compare. if it's close, buy the individual items — you end up with exactly what you use.

## material, not table

**the pangea and utility series bundles differ by material, not by which table they fit.** both attach to the same magnetic rail, and the pangea and tavern share that rail — so either bundle works on either table. the pangea bundles are the solid-oak line; the utility series bundles are the hard-wearing café-grade line. choose by durability and look. see [which accessories fit my table?](which-accessories-fit-my-table.md).

h:
buying a zola table as a gift you can ship to someone else's address, but freight needs an adult 18+ there to receive it — so a surprise delivery is hard to keep secret. # buying a zola table as a gift

you can absolutely ship to someone else's address. there are two things about freight that make gifting a table different from gifting a parcel, and both are worth knowing before you order.

## the recipient has to be there

tables ship by freight, not parcel. **an adult 18 or older must be present to receive the delivery**, the carrier calls ahead to schedule an appointment window, and the recipient may be asked to help the driver unload.

that's hard to square with a surprise. a few ways people handle it:

- **tell them, but not what it is.** "something big is arriving thursday, be home" preserves most of the surprise.
- **ship it to yourself** and move it later — bearing in mind it's 133–242 lbs in about three cartons.
- **ship to a willing accomplice** at a different address.

what doesn't work is scheduling a freight delivery to someone who doesn't know it's coming.

## timing, honestly

if you're buying for a specific date, work from **the ship date on the product page**, then add **7–10 business days of transit**, then the carrier's scheduling call on top.

most tables are on pre-order, and the ship date lives on the product page rather than in a general promise — it's the number we keep current. if the date on the page is tight against your occasion, message us through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us) before ordering and we'll tell you honestly whether it'll land in time.

we'd rather talk you out of a date we can't hit than have it arrive in january.

## it arrives unassembled

the table comes in cartons and needs building — see [how long assembly takes and what you need](how-long-assembly-takes-and-what-you-need.md). it's not a gift that gets used the evening it lands, and the flip step wants two people.

if the occasion matters more than the surprise, some people give a printed card and build it together that weekend.

## accessories are easier

cup holders, trays, organizers, play mats, and the storage cubes all ship parcel — no appointment, no signature, no assembly. if you want something that arrives cleanly on a date, an accessory for a table they already own is a much simpler gift than a table.

h:
changing or cancelling your order address, size, finish, added items, and cancellations can usually change before your order ships — reach out through our contact page with your order number as soon as you can. # changing or cancelling your order

most changes — cancelling, resizing, changing finish, editing the shipping address, adding items — are possible up until your order ships. the real cutoff is when the freight shipment gets booked, not when you placed the order, so a pre-order often has a lot of room. reach out through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us) with your order number and what you'd like changed, as soon as you can.

## what we need from you

- your **order number**
- the **email on the order**
- what you'd like changed — the more specific, the faster we can act

## before it ships — the easy window

while your order is still processing, we can typically:

- cancel it
- change the size, finish, or leg height
- correct the shipping address
- add or remove accessories

speed matters here more than anything else — the sooner your message lands, the more likely we catch it before the order is staged for freight.

## shipping address

changeable **before freight is booked**. once a carrier has the shipment and an address, redirecting it becomes a carrier reroute rather than a simple edit — sometimes possible, sometimes not, and it can add cost and delay. if you've moved or mistyped an address, tell us immediately rather than waiting to see whether it matters.

## size or finish

usually possible before shipping, with two things to know:

- **it may change your ship date.** switching to something on a different pre-order timeline means inheriting that timeline — we'll tell you the new date before making the change.
- **it's an edit, not a return** — much simpler than receiving a table and sending it back. see [returning a table](returning-a-table.md) if the table has already arrived.

## adding items

often yes, especially if the original order hasn't shipped — and adding accessories to an existing table order saves you a second delivery. if it can't be added (usually because the order is already being processed), a separate order is the fallback, and we'll say so rather than leaving it ambiguous.

## splitting a mixed order

by default, an order containing a table and accessories together **ships together**. if you'd rather have the accessories now and the table when it's ready, ask — we can usually split it. worth doing if the table is on a longer pre-order date and you want the accessories in the meantime.

## holding an order

moving house, travelling, or otherwise not ready to receive a 242 lb freight delivery? we can **hold the order** until a date you give us — much better than a delivery arriving at an empty house.

## once the freight shipment is in motion

after a table is handed to the carrier, changes get considerably harder — a shipment already on a truck generally has to complete its route. **refusing a delivery to cancel an order can incur return freight charges**, so don't refuse on impulse if you no longer want it. get in touch first and we'll walk you through the options, including our standard return path.

## cancelling

also possible before shipment. payment is taken at order, so a cancellation is a refund rather than a voided charge — see [how refunds work](how-refunds-work.md).

## changed your mind after delivery?

that's a return, not a cancellation. you have **30 days from delivery** — see [zola return policy](zola-return-policy.md).

h:
caring for your zola finish soft dry or barely damp cloth, mild dish soap and water when it needs more, nothing stronger — and the visible grain and lighter lines in cerused oak are intentional, not a defect. # caring for your zola finish

two things: how to clean it, and one thing about cerused oak that catches people off guard.

## the cerused oak look is intentional

the **cerused oak** finish is meant to have visible grain with lighter lines worked into the oak. that texture is part of the look — it's what ceruse is — rather than a defect, a manufacturing inconsistency, or weathering. if you were expecting a uniform surface, the first impression can read as "this looks worn," and it isn't.

grain pattern also varies naturally piece to piece, which is a feature of real wood finishes generally.

if a finish genuinely looks wrong to you after that — not textured, but *wrong* — send us a photo through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us) and we'll take a look.

## day-to-day care

- wipe with a **soft, dry or barely damp cloth**
- when water alone won't shift something, use **mild dish soap and water**
- **avoid anything stronger** — no solvents, no abrasives, no strong household sprays
- **avoid standing liquid.** wipe spills rather than letting them sit
- use the **cup holders** for drinks. that's largely what they're for, and it's the single easiest way to keep the play surface pristine

## where the table can live: indoors, climate-controlled

this one matters more than any cleaning habit. **zola tables belong in a normal heated and cooled indoor room** — nowhere else.

the tables are built from solid oak, oak veneer, and premium mdf, and all three move with humidity. a garage, an unheated basement, a sunroom, or a covered patio swings too far in temperature and moisture across a year. what that looks like after a season or two is veneer lifting at an edge, panels that stop sitting flush, and finish damage — and because it comes from the environment rather than the manufacturing, none of it is covered by the warranty.

two things to watch even indoors:

- **direct sunlight** fades a finish unevenly, and the part under a play mat or a topper fades at a different rate than the part that's exposed.
- **direct heat** — a radiator, a wood stove, or a vent blowing straight onto the table — dries wood out locally and is the fastest way to open a seam.

if your only available room is marginal, ask us before you order rather than after. message us through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us) and describe the space.

## if you scratch or ding it

a **color-matched furniture touch-up marker or wax stick** is the right tool, and any furniture or hardware store carries them. two rules make the difference between an invisible repair and a worse mark:

1. **match in person.** take a photo of your table into the store — dark walnut and cerused oak are both harder to match from memory than you'd expect.
2. **test somewhere hidden first.** an underside, or an inside edge. never test on the spot you're trying to fix.

**don't sand it.** the visible surfaces are oak veneer, and the veneer layer is thin — sanding through it turns a scratch into something genuinely difficult to recover from. this is a fill-and-blend job, not a refinishing job. we don't sell a branded touch-up kit, and we'd rather point you at the right generic product than pretend otherwise.

minor scratches and dents are cosmetic wear, not defects, so they sit outside warranty coverage — see [wear versus a defect](wear-versus-a-defect.md). if a mark looks like something other than ordinary damage, send a photo through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us) and we'll take a look.

## protecting the surface long-term

- the **table topper set** protects the recessed vault when the table is doing dining or work duty — see [what the table topper set does](what-the-table-topper-set-does.md)
- the **table topper storage cube** ($129.99) keeps the topper panels in padded inserts when they're off the table, rather than leaning against a wall collecting scuffs
- a **zola tristar grid play mat** (5mm neoprene, rubber backing) gives the play surface a working layer for games with a lot of piece movement

## what the warranty says about finish

cosmetic damage — scratches, dents, and colour fading — isn't covered, which is standard for furniture finishes. **a manufacturing defect in the finish is**, and the two are genuinely different: a finish lifting or separating isn't wear, whereas a scratch is. natural wood variation, including the cerused oak texture above, is explicitly not a defect. see [zola warranty coverage](zola-warranty-coverage.md) and [wear versus a defect](wear-versus-a-defect.md).

choosing your leg height standard (26" clearance) suits dining chairs and is the default; counter (32") needs stools; coffee (14") is for lounge seating. # choosing your leg height

three heights are available, and the option name refers to the **clearance underneath** rather than the overall table height.

| option | clearance underneath | overall height | pairs with |
|---|---|---|---|
| **standard** | 26″ | **30.5″** | dining chairs — the default |
| **counter** | 32″ | **36.5″** | counter stools |
| **coffee** | 14″ | **18.5″** | sofa and lounge seating |

the tabletop adds 4.5″ over the clearance figure in every configuration, so overall height is always clearance + 4.5″.

standard is what most people want. at 30.5″ overall that's normal dining-table height, and it's what our **pangea mid-century dining chairs** are made for.

counter legs add **$100**.

## choose seating and height together

this is the one that trips people up. **our dining chairs suit the standard height only.** we don't sell counter stools or lounge seating, so if you choose counter or coffee you're sourcing seating elsewhere — and that's much easier to plan before the table arrives than after.

- **counter (32″)** — 36.5″ overall, so you'll want stools with roughly a 24–26″ seat height. standing players are comfortable at this height too, which is part of the appeal for a games room.
- **coffee (14″)** — 18.5″ overall, designed for playing from a sofa or floor cushions. it's a genuinely different way to use the table, and not one that works for long sessions with a big game.

## changing height later

legs are sold separately — **$150** for standard and coffee, **$250** for counter — so a height change later is a leg swap rather than a new table.

before ordering a replacement set, message us through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us) with your table size and what you're trying to end up with. leg sets are handled case by case and it's worth confirming the fit for your configuration first.

## if you're using it as a dining table

h:
connecting two pangea tables rails lift off any edge, so two pangeas join into one surface — two 3×5s make a 3×10.5 or a 6.5×5. # connecting two pangea tables

the pangea is modular on purpose. **the rails lift off any edge**, so two tables can be brought together into a single continuous playing surface rather than sitting as two tables pushed against each other.

## what two 3×5s give you

remove the rails on the edge where they meet, and two 3×5 tables become:

- **3 × 10.5** — joined end to end, for a long table
- **6.5 × 5** — joined side by side, for a wide one

the joined dimension isn't simply double, because removing the shared rails reclaims the space those rails occupied.

## what to expect

**tune the rails after joining.** this is the same alignment pass a single table needs out of the box, and it matters more across a seam — the two surfaces have to agree. walk through [tuning your pangea after assembly](tuning-your-pangea-after-assembly.md), paying particular attention to the vertical alignment step so accessories slide across the join without catching.

**play mats stay per-table.** mats are cut to a single vault's playable area, so a joined configuration uses each table's own mat rather than one large mat spanning the seam.

**rail accessories are unaffected.** cup holders, trays, and other omnitrack items clamp to whatever rail remains, so they move to the outer edges of the combined surface.

## a table doesn't change size on its own

worth being clear, because "modular" gets read two ways: **joining a second table is the expansion path.** a 3×3 doesn't become a 3×5 by adding parts — the size you buy is the size that table stays. what you can do is put two of them together.

## planning a combined setup

two things worth measuring before you commit:

- **floor space.** add the overall footprints, not the playable areas — and leave clearance to walk and seat players around the outside.
- **which edges you'll join.** this decides whether you end up long or wide, and it's easier to decide before assembly than after.

if you're buying a second table specifically to combine it, send us your current model and what you're trying to end up with through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us), and we'll confirm the configuration works before you order.

tables move by freight, and international freight on a piece of furniture this size runs into the thousands. that isn't a cost we'd feel good handing to a customer, and shipping something premium halfway around the world on a route we haven't proven is how tables arrive damaged. we'd rather do it properly than do it early.

we're **aiming to open up international shipping in late 2026**. we're not going to promise a date, a country list, or a rate until we can actually stand behind them — but it's an active project, not a someday.

freight delivery and scheduling tables ship ltl freight (usually abf) curbside with liftgate included, and the carrier calls to schedule a delivery appointment — plan to be there, and inspect the shipment before you sign. # freight delivery and scheduling

your table arrives on a truck, not in a parcel van. zola tables are heavy, premium furniture, and they ship **ltl freight** — usually with **abf**. here's how that works so nothing about delivery day is a surprise.

## the carrier calls you

once your order ships, you'll get a confirmation email with tracking. then the freight carrier reaches out directly — by phone or email — to arrange a **delivery appointment**. you'll know your window in advance rather than waiting on a truck all day.

two things worth doing when they call:

1. **pick a window you can actually be there for.** freight delivery needs an adult 18+ to receive and sign for the shipment.
2. **mention anything awkward about your address** — a steep or long driveway, a gravel approach, no room for a large truck to turn. better raised on the scheduling call than discovered by a driver.

## what's included: curbside with liftgate

delivery is **curbside, with liftgate service included**. the truck's powered platform lowers the shipment to ground level, so nothing has to come off the truck by hand and there's no liftgate fee to arrange.

the driver leaves it at the kerb or the end of your driveway. moving it from there into the house is yours, and the cartons are long and heavy enough that a second person makes a real difference — see [receiving your freight delivery](receiving-your-freight-delivery.md) for the weights and what to check on the day.

## inspect before you sign

this is the one step that matters most, and it takes two minutes.

before you sign the delivery paperwork, walk around the shipment and look at the packaging. if the boxes or pallet show visible damage — crushed corners, punctures, a shifted load — **note that on the delivery paperwork even if you go ahead and accept the shipment**. that note is what preserves a claim against the carrier. if something is severely damaged, you can refuse the shipment outright and mark it "refused due to damage in transit."

most shipping damage isn't caught until the boxes are open, which is completely normal and still fully covered — see [my order arrived damaged](my-order-arrived-damaged.md) for that path. but if the driver is still standing there, the two-minute look is worth it.

## transit time

once the table leaves our warehouse, expect **7-10 business days in transit**, then the scheduling call. processing time before that depends on whether the item is in stock or on pre-order — see [how long does my zola table take to ship?](how-long-does-my-zola-table-take-to-ship.md).

## accessories

smaller items — flex inserts, cup holders, trays, mats — don't need freight and don't need a delivery appointment. only the tables and larger components move by truck.

how long assembly takes and what you need customer-assembled, and much easier with a second person — mainly for flipping the table upright once the legs are on. # how long assembly takes and what you need

zola tables are **customer-assembled**. there's no technician visit and no white-glove build — the table arrives in cartons and you put it together where it's going to live.

## get a second person for the flip

you can do most of the build alone. the part that genuinely wants two people is **turning the table upright once the legs are attached**.

the frame goes together face-down, the legs bolt on from underneath, and then the whole assembly has to be flipped. a 3×3 is 133 lbs, a 3×5 is 182 lbs, and a 4×6 is 242 lbs — a flip at that weight is awkward alone and risks the finish, the floor, and your back.

if you're building solo, line up someone for that one step.

## assemble it in the room it will live in

once it's built, a pangea doesn't fit through a standard doorway without coming apart again. build it where it's staying.

worth checking the route **before** delivery day too — the longest carton is about 47″ on a 3×3, 71″ on a 3×5, and 83″ on a 4×6. those are the numbers that matter for a tight stairwell or a turn in a hallway.

## order of operations matters

the one thing worth knowing before you start: **leave the bolts snug rather than fully tightened until the table is flipped upright.** bolts fully torqued face-down lock in whatever alignment gravity gave you, and the rails and legs both need a tuning pass once the table is on its feet.

full walkthrough in [tuning your pangea after assembly](tuning-your-pangea-after-assembly.md). it's worth reading that one *before* you start rather than after.

## instructions

instructions are sent per model rather than printed in the carton. if you don't have them, message us through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us) with your order number and we'll send the right set — see [where are my assembly instructions?](where-are-my-assembly-instructions.md).

- **hardware looks missing.** it ships with the legs and frame, not loose. see [where is the assembly hardware?](where-is-the-assembly-hardware.md).
- **the 3×5 centre section won't line up.** it installs one way only — rotate it 180° and the holes meet.
- **rails don't sit flush.** expected out of the box, and it's a tuning step rather than a fault.

freight tracing is much more effective early. terminals move a lot of pallets, and a misrouted shipment is far easier to find while its trail is fresh than a fortnight later. carriers also have windows for filing claims.

- tracking hasn't moved in several business days
- a promised delivery window came and went with no carrier contact
- tracking says delivered and nothing arrived
- part of a multi-carton shipment arrived and part didn't
- the carrier says it was delivered to an address that isn't yours

any of those, tell us.

t: My table wobbles or feels uneven
d: Almost always hardware that isn't fully tightened — and the one people miss is the bolt that runs down through the table surface into the leg.
h:
my table wobbles or feels uneven almost always hardware that isn't fully tightened — and the one people miss is the bolt that runs down through the table surface into the leg. # my table wobbles or feels uneven

this is nearly always an assembly issue rather than a fault, and it comes down to hardware that isn't fully tightened. work through the checks below before anything else — most wobble resolves here.

## check every bolt in the legs

**go around all of them, not just the ones you can see from underneath.**

the one people miss is the **bolt that runs down through the top of the table surface into the leg**. it's easy to overlook because it's on the playing side rather than underneath with the others, and a leg that's snug on its under-table bolts can still move if that top bolt is loose. check it on every leg.

then confirm the **two bolts securing each leg from underneath** are tight as well. all of them, every leg.

## check the bolts joining the sections

on a table with multiple sections, the **three bolts joining them** need to be fully tightened. sections that aren't pulled tight against each other let the whole table flex, which reads as a wobble even when every leg is solid.

if you're not sure these were done in the right order, [tuning your pangea after assembly](tuning-your-pangea-after-assembly.md) walks through it — bolts should be left snug until the table is flipped upright, then fully tightened.

## retighten after a week

hardware settles under load. a pass around every bolt after the table has been in use for a week takes a couple of minutes and catches a fair number of small wobbles. worth repeating periodically regardless.

## rule out the floor

quick to check and easy to miss: try the table in a different spot, or slide a shim under one leg. an uneven floor produces exactly the same rock as a table problem, and older houses and floating floors are common culprits.

## if it still moves

if every bolt is tight — including the top-down leg bolts — the sections are pulled together, and it isn't the floor, submit a claim at [zolamod.com/pages/claims-form](https://zolamod.com/pages/claims-form).

include your table size and leg height, and a short video showing the movement if you can. a video is worth several paragraphs of description here, because *how* it moves tells us more than *that* it moves.

## don't overtighten

if tightening to snug hasn't fixed it, more force won't. overtightening can strip an insert, which is a much bigger repair than whatever you're chasing.

they're not two sizes of the same idea. they're built differently, for different rooms.

## the short version

**pangea** if you want a dedicated gaming table with a recessed vault, in a home, at a fixed height.

**tavern** if you want height adjustment — a table that works seated and standing, in a space that changes use through the day.

## side by side

| | pangea | tavern |
|---|---|---|
| sizes | 3×3, 3×5, 4×6 | 44×30, 44×60 |
| height | fixed — 26″ clearance standard | **adjustable, 29″–44.5″** |
| recessed vault | yes, 2.5″ deep | no — 1.25″ rail |
| finishes | dark walnut, cerused oak | smoked walnut |
| rails | solid malaysian oak, omnitrack magnetic rail | steel frame, same magnetic rail (flex-compatible) |
| toppers | magnetic table topper set | — |
| accessories | oak or utility line + flex (shared rail) | oak or utility line + flex (shared rail) |

**the vault.** a pangea's 2.5″ recess is the whole point — the game sits down in it, pieces don't get knocked off the edge, and the topper set closes it into a flat dining surface. the tavern doesn't have that; it's a flat playing surface with a low rail.

**height adjustment.** the tavern raises and lowers. for a café where staff reconfigure, or a room that's a games table some evenings and a standing work surface others, that flexibility is worth more than the vault.

**weight and permanence.** a pangea is heavy and stays where it's built. a tavern is a third to half the weight and easier to move and reconfigure.

h:
play mats explained every pangea ships with a mat sized for its vault. the standalone mat skus are for replacements and spares, and are a separate thing. # play mats explained

**every pangea comes with a play mat sized for its vault.** you don't need to buy one to use your table — it's included, in the right size, whichever table you bought.

that's the part people get confused about, because mats also appear as products you can buy on their own.

## two different things

**the mat that ships with your table** is included, matched to your vault, and arrives in the box.

**the standalone mat listings** are for replacements and spares — a second mat, or one to replace a mat that's been through a few hundred sessions. those are sold separately:

| mat | price |
|---|---|
| zola tristar grid play mat (3×3) | $59.99 |
| zola tristar grid play mat (3×5) | $69.99 |

if you don't see a standalone listing matching your table size, that doesn't mean your table shipped without one. it means we don't currently stock that size as a separate item. ask us through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us) and we'll sort out a replacement.

## what the mat is

**5 mm neoprene with a rubber backing**, in space gray, printed with the tristar grid. it's made to sit down in the recessed vault rather than lie on top of a flat surface — that's why the edges meet the rails cleanly instead of curling.

neoprene does the two things a gaming surface needs: dice don't bounce off it, and cards can be picked up from it.

## it's meant to wear

the mat is the part that takes the abrasion — dice landing, miniatures sliding, boxes dragged across. that's its job, and it's why it's inexpensive to replace relative to the table underneath.

treat a worn mat as a consumable rather than a fault. a worn vault floor would be a different matter, which is the point of having the mat there.

## letting a new one settle

mats ship rolled. lay it flat in the vault, grid side up, for a few hours at room temperature before judging the fit — neoprene holds a curl, and a curled edge reads as a mat that's too big.

if it still doesn't sit flat after that, the usual cause is the table rather than the mat — see [why my play mat doesn't fit](why-my-play-mat-doesnt-fit.md).

h:
protecting your table surface the play mat takes the wear, cup holders keep drinks off the surface entirely, and lifting rather than dragging avoids most of the rest. # protecting your table surface

most surface wear on a gaming table comes from four things: dice, drinks, dragging, and sunlight. all four are avoidable.

## let the mat take the wear

the neoprene **tristar grid play mat** sits in the vault and is the single most effective thing you can do. dice land on it, miniatures slide on it, and it absorbs the abrasion the vault floor would otherwise take.

it's also the cheapest part to replace. that's the point — a worn mat is a consumable; a worn vault floor is a table.

## keep drinks off the surface entirely

**cup holders clip into the omnitrack rail**, which puts the glass beside the table rather than on it. between a knocked drink and a ring mark, that's the whole problem solved rather than mitigated.

if you're using the table for meals with the toppers fitted, coasters and trivets still apply — see [using your table for dining](using-your-table-for-dining.md).

## lift, don't drag

drag a heavy box across a finish and it will mark, on any table at any price. lifting game boxes, laptops, and boards on and off matters more than any product you can buy.

same for the toppers: lift them into place rather than sliding them across the rails.

## keep it out of direct sun

fading is one of the things every furniture warranty excludes, including ours — and it's cumulative, invisible day to day, and irreversible. a table by a south-facing window will change colour over a year or two, and unevenly.

if the room can't avoid it, a blind at the worst hours does more than anything applied to the wood.

## what counts as wear rather than a defect

scratches, dents, and fading from use are wear. a finish flaw that arrived that way is a defect. the line is whether it was there when you received the table — see [something is defective or not fitting right](something-is-defective-or-not-fitting-right.md) if you're unsure which you're looking at, and send a photo; that settles it faster than a description.

receiving your freight delivery curbside with liftgate, on a scheduled appointment, adult 18+ present — inspect everything before you sign, because signing clean makes a damage claim much harder. # receiving your freight delivery

a table arrives on a freight truck, not a parcel van. three things about that are worth knowing before the day.

## someone 18 or over has to be there

the carrier calls ahead to book an appointment window, and **an adult 18+ must be present** to receive and sign. this isn't a delivery that can be left on a porch.

## it's curbside, and the liftgate is included

**liftgate service comes with every table delivery.** the truck has a powered platform that lowers the shipment to ground level, so it isn't coming off the truck by hand and you don't need to arrange or pay for a liftgate separately.

what that gets you is the shipment on the ground at the kerb or the end of your driveway. it is **not** threshold, room-of-choice, or white-glove — the driver isn't bringing boxes inside, up stairs, or unpacking anything.

**getting the cartons from the curb into the house is yours.** plan for it: a 4×6 is 242 lbs across roughly three cartons, and the longest is about 83″. have a second person there — ideally the same one who'll help you flip the table during assembly.

## inspect before you sign — this is the important one

short answer: **damage that happened in transit is not a warranty claim** — and the other route is faster for you.

## the dividing line

| what happened | which path | how to start it |
|---|---|---|
| **arrived damaged** — cracked, crushed, scuffed in shipping | damage flow — **within 5 days of delivery** | photos of the damage, the carton, and the shipping label + order number through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us) |
| **failed or defective in normal use** — within the coverage period for that component | warranty claim | warranty claim form on [zolamod.com/pages/warranty-policy](https://zolamod.com/pages/warranty-policy) |
| **missing or broken part in the box** | parts flow | photo + order number through our contact page |

## the 5-day window on transit damage

**shipping damage has to be reported within 5 days of delivery.** that deadline isn't ours — it's what the carrier's claims process requires, and it's why we can't do much about damage surfaced weeks later.

two practical consequences:

- **open and check everything promptly**, even if you're not assembling for a while. a carton that looks fine outside can hold a cracked panel.
- **keep the packaging** until you've checked it all. photos of the outer carton and shipping label are part of the claim, and once the boxes are flattened that evidence is gone.

## why transit damage goes the other way

the warranty covers **manufacturing defects** — an inadequacy in materials or workmanship that existed when you received the product. damage from transport, loading, unloading, or handling is explicitly excluded, because it isn't a defect in the product.

that's not a dead end, though. it's a different, quicker desk. we don't need a claim form, a proof-of-purchase review, or a 3-5 business day evaluation window to send you a replacement part for a piece that got crushed on a truck. photos and an order number are enough.

## what to send

send us your order number and **clear photos of the damaged area** through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us):

1. close-up shots of the damage
2. the shipping label
3. the boxes and packaging, if possible

the shipping label is the one people forget, and it's the piece that identifies the shipment when we take it up with the carrier.

full walkthrough: [my order arrived damaged](my-order-arrived-damaged.md).

reach out through our contact page and describe what you're seeing with a photo. we'll route it correctly. you won't lose time by picking the "wrong" one first.

d: Pangea rails are modular, so they often need a short alignment pass out of the box — tighten the section bolts snug, flip the table, align the rails, then fully tighten.
h:
tuning your pangea after assembly pangea rails are modular, so they often need a short alignment pass out of the box — tighten the section bolts snug, flip the table, align the rails, then fully tighten. # tuning your pangea after assembly

the pangea is built to come apart. rails lift off any edge so two tables can join into one larger surface later, and that modularity is the whole point of the design — but it also means the sections arrive aligned *well*, not aligned *perfectly*. a short tuning pass at the end of assembly is normal and expected, not a sign something is wrong.

budget five minutes for it. it's the difference between accessories that glide and accessories that catch.

## do this in the right order

the single most common mistake is tightening everything down before the table is flipped upright. bolts that are fully torqued face-down lock in whatever alignment gravity gave you. leave things snug, flip, *then* tighten.

## 1. center section orientation (3×5 only)

the center 2-foot section of a 3×5 installs **one way only**.

before you bolt anything, check that the bolt holes line up. if they don't, rotate the center section **180 degrees** and they will. nothing is mismatched — the section simply has a front and a back.

## 2. rail alignment

two different symptoms, two different fixes.

**rails don't line up vertically** — one section's rail sits slightly higher than its neighbor, so accessories catch or won't slide across the seam.

1. tighten the **three bolts** holding the sections together until they're **snug, not fully tightened**.
2. flip the table upright.
3. check the vertical alignment of the rails and adjust as needed.
4. now fully tighten the three bolts.

**a rail's outward face isn't flush** with the rail beside it.

1. lightly loosen the **two bolts underneath the table** that secure that rail section.
2. adjust the rail's position until the faces sit flush.
3. retighten.

## 3. leg alignment

same principle as the rails — don't commit before the flip.

when installing the legs, leave the **two bolts that secure the leg underneath** loose. flip the table upright, tune the alignment, tighten the bolt that goes **through the top** of the table first, then tighten the two leg bolts underneath.

## why this matters more than it sounds

the play vault is sized to its stated playable area exactly — 36″ × 36″ on a 3×3, 36″ × 60″ on a 3×5, 48″ × 72″ on a 4×6. there's no slack designed in. if the sections aren't pulled fully together, the opening ends up a fraction short, and a play mat cut to the correct size won't lie flat in it.

so if your mat seems slightly too long, tune the rails first. see [why my play mat doesn't fit](why-my-play-mat-doesnt-fit.md).

## if it still isn't right

if the rails won't come flush, a bolt won't thread, or something is visibly bent or missing, stop and send us a photo through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us) with your order number. don't force a fastener — a stripped insert is a much bigger repair than whatever you're working around.

yes. fitting the **table topper set** converts the recessed vault into a flat, continuous surface, and that's exactly what it's designed for — the table works as a dining or work table between games rather than being a single-purpose piece.

## use trivets under anything hot

the surface has a durable low-gloss coating that resists scratches, glare, and spills. it is **not** a heat-proof surface.

put a trivet or mat under hot pans, serving dishes, and anything straight from an oven or hob. zola's own care guidance is explicit about avoiding direct heat, and heat damage to a finish isn't a manufacturing defect — it's the one kind of surface damage that's genuinely hard to put right.

warm plates are fine. a cast-iron pot out of the oven is not.

## spills

blot promptly rather than letting liquid sit. the coating is spill-resistant, which buys you time — it doesn't make standing liquid harmless, particularly at a seam or an edge.

the toppers are described as leak-resistant, but treat that as protection against a knocked drink rather than a guarantee that nothing reaches the vault. if something substantial goes over, lift the topper and check underneath rather than assuming.

more detail in [protecting your table surface](protecting-your-table-surface.md).

## cleaning

soft, dry cloth for routine cleaning; slightly damp for anything that needs it. when water alone won't shift something, **mild dish soap and water** is the right step up.

go no stronger than that without asking us first. **avoid harsh cleaners** — solvents, abrasives, and strong household sprays. cleaning-agent damage sits outside warranty coverage, and it's entirely avoidable.

d: A defect was there when the table reached you. Wear is what use adds. If you're unsure, send a photo — that settles it faster than a description.
h:
wear versus a defect a defect was there when the table reached you. wear is what use adds. if you're unsure, send a photo — that settles it faster than a description. # wear versus a defect

the useful test isn't how bad something looks. it's **when it started**.

> a **defect** is a flaw in materials or workmanship that existed when you received the table.
> **wear** is what use adds afterwards.

that distinction decides which path a problem takes, and it's why we ask for photos early — a mark that was there on day one and a mark that appeared in month eight look identical in isolation.

## usually a defect

- a panel that never sat flush, from the first assembly
- magnets misaligned or missing, so blocks won't seat correctly
- hardware that won't thread, or arrived bent
- a finish flaw present before the table was used
- a component that doesn't match its published dimensions

## usually wear

- scratches, dents, and marks accumulated through use
- imprinting from dice, miniatures, or writing on the surface
- fading from sunlight
- wear on the play surface, mat, or armrest materials
- loosening hardware that retightens fine

wear isn't a judgement about how you've treated the table — it's what furniture does. it's excluded from warranty coverage on essentially every piece of furniture sold, ours included.

## the genuinely ambiguous ones

some things sit between, and those are worth sending in rather than deciding yourself:

- **wobble** that appeared after a few months — could be settling, could be assembly, could be something else. see [my table wobbles](my-table-wobbles.md).
- **a panel that used to sit flush and now doesn't** — the change over time is the interesting part.
- **finish lifting or separating** rather than being scratched — separation isn't usually wear.

photograph it, tell us roughly when you first noticed it, and let us look.

## damage in transit is neither

freight damage isn't a warranty claim and isn't wear — it's a faster, separate path with its own process. don't file it as a warranty issue; you'll get a slower answer for no reason. see [shipping damage vs. warranty claim](shipping-damage-vs-warranty-claim.md).

## when in doubt, just ask

you're not expected to adjudicate your own claim. send a photo, your order number, and when you noticed it, through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us). working out which category it falls into is our job.

the **table topper set** is a set of precision-fit, magnet-held panels that drop over the recessed play vault to give you a flat, level surface — a gaming table on game night, a dining or work table the rest of the week, without moving anything into a closet.

## how it works

the panels are **held in place by magnets** — set them in and they seat flush. removing them takes seconds, and the game underneath is still exactly where you left it, which is the quiet advantage of a recessed vault: a campaign in progress can stay set up under a dinner.

## sizing and finish

topper sets are sold **per table size** and in **dark walnut or cerused oak** to match your table. a topper for one size will not fit another — see [which accessories fit my table?](which-accessories-fit-my-table.md).

| table size | table topper set |
|---|---|
| 3×3 | $300 |
| 3×5 | $400 |
| 4×6 | sold and invoiced separately — ask through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us) to confirm current availability |

**ordering a mismatched finish** — dark walnut toppers on a cerused oak table, or the reverse — is possible, but not through checkout. ask for a human in the chat on our site; our team configures the order manually and emails you an invoice to pay. we handle it that way because a mixed-finish set is a deliberate choice rather than a mistake, and we'd rather confirm it with you than have a mismatched set arrive as a surprise.

## where the panels go when they're off the table

they're solid, veneered, and finished on the visible face — leaning them against a wall works for an evening, but it's not where you want them living.

the **table topper storage cube** ($129.99) is the purpose-built answer: a padded oak cube sized to hold the panels upright, protected, and out of the way rather than stacked on a floor. the **storage cube xl** ($199.99) does the same job with more room, and also takes **table leaves and dividers** as well as toppers — the one to get if you run a configuration with extension leaves or use dividers regularly.

if you're not buying a cube yet, some things are worth doing regardless:

- **store panels upright, not stacked flat** — weight on a stack presses grit into the faces
- **keep something soft between panels** — a blanket or felt; face-to-face contact with nothing between them is how the finish gets marked
- **avoid damp or hot storage** — a garage that swings between humid and freezing is unkind to a veneered panel; the panels are veneered specifically for dimensional stability, and extreme storage undoes that
- **keep them out of direct sun** — fading is excluded from warranty coverage, and a panel that's faded unevenly against the rest of the set is very visible once it goes back in

the need for topper storage isn't obvious from the product page, and people often discover it after the table arrives. if you know you'll switch between game and dining use regularly, it's worth adding the cube to the same order as your table — accessories ship parcel, so consolidating avoids a second delivery.

h:
what zola tables are made of commercial-grade, high-density engineered wood with a real-wood finish in dark walnut or cerused oak — solid and heavy, which is also why the tables ship by freight. # what zola tables are made of

a pangea is three materials, each chosen for the job it does:

- **frame and legs — industrial powder-coated steel.** the structure is metal, not wood. that's where the stability and most of the weight come from.
- **rails — solid malaysian oak.** the perimeter you touch, lean on, and clamp accessories to is solid hardwood.
- **toppers and base panels — premium mdf with a premium oak veneer.** real oak over a dense engineered core.

**the table is not solid oak, and we won't tell you it is.** the wide flat parts are veneered panels, and that's a deliberate choice rather than a cost saving — see below.

they are premium, built-to-last pieces: heavy and dense, which is a large part of why they feel the way they do in a room. it's also why they ship by freight rather than parcel.

## why veneer on the wide parts

the toppers and panels are the one place a veneered core is genuinely the right call. a veneered panel is dimensionally stable, so precision-fit topper panels stay flat and stay aligned instead of moving with seasonal humidity. that stability is what lets the table topper set drop in level, and what keeps the magnets seating properly over years of use.

solid wood that wide would cup and swell with the seasons, and the magnetic fit would drift with it. a gaming table that relies on panels meeting flush is exactly the wrong place for a material that moves.

the rails don't have that problem — they're narrow enough that solid oak stays true, so that's what's used there.

## accessories are solid oak

the standard pangea accessory line — including the standard flex tray — is **solid oak**, not veneer. those pieces are small enough that movement isn't a concern, and they're handled constantly, so solid stock is the better material.

the **utility series** versions are the exception: that's the hard-wearing line built for cafés and high-traffic use, and it isn't oak. see [which accessories fit my table?](which-accessories-fit-my-table.md).

## finishes

two finishes are available across the pangea line:

- **dark walnut** — deep and even
- **cerused oak** — open grain with lighter lines worked into it; the visible texture is intentional and part of the look

the **tavern sit-stand** line comes in **smoked walnut**.

component pieces — table topper sets, panels — are offered in the matching finishes so a later addition still looks like it came with the table.

## the omnitrack rail

the magnetic perimeter rail around the play surface is the **omnitrack** system. it's what cup holders, flex trays, and flex inserts snap into, and it's what adds about 3.25 inches (8.3 cm) per side to the overall footprint. see [playable size vs. overall footprint](playable-size-vs-overall-footprint.md).

## caring for it

wipe with a soft, dry or barely damp cloth. avoid harsh cleaners and standing liquid. full guidance: [caring for your zola finish](caring-for-your-zola-finish.md).

h:
where is my order, and tracking your delivery reach out through our contact page with your order number to check status; freight tracking moves in fewer, larger steps than parcel, so a quiet day or two is normal. # where is my order, and tracking your delivery

happy to check anytime — reach out through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us) with your **order number** and the **email address on the order** and we'll tell you exactly where it stands. below is the full path an order takes, what's normal at each stage, and how freight tracking differs from a parcel's.

## the path from order to delivery

1. **order confirmation — immediately.** you get a confirmation email with your order number right away. keep it handy — it's what we ask for on replacement parts, returns, and warranty claims.
2. **processing — timing depends on stock status.**
   - **pre-order items** (most tables right now): the estimated ship date is listed **on that product's own page**, and we keep it current as inventory lands. go by that date.
   - **in stock, normal conditions:** about **1 week** to process.
   - **in stock, right after a restock:** closer to **3 weeks**, while we work through the backorder queue in order.
3. **shipping confirmation and tracking.** tables ship **ltl freight** (typically **abf**); accessories ship **parcel**. you'll get tracking by email the moment it ships.
4. **transit — 7 to 10 business days**, standard once it's on the truck.
5. **the carrier calls to schedule.** for freight, the carrier contacts you directly to set a **delivery appointment**, so you know your window ahead of time. plan to have someone there to receive and sign, and arrange help to move the boxes inside — freight delivery is generally to the curb or driveway.
6. **delivery day — the two-minute inspection.** before you sign, look over the packaging. note any visible damage to the boxes or pallet on the delivery paperwork **even if you accept the shipment** — that's what preserves a carrier claim. refuse outright only if it's severely damaged.
7. **unboxing and assembly.** most shipping damage actually turns up here, not at the curb, and it's completely normal and fully handled: send clear photos of the damaged area (including close-up shots), the shipping label, and the boxes/packaging if possible, along with your order number, through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us) and we'll ship a replacement. need the assembly instructions or can't locate the hardware? see [where are my assembly instructions?](where-are-my-assembly-instructions.md) and [where is the assembly hardware?](where-is-the-assembly-hardware.md).

## what "on track" looks like

| stage | what you should have | typical duration |
|---|---|---|
| order placed | confirmation email with order number | immediate |
| processing | nothing new yet — this is the quiet stretch | product page date, or ~1 week in stock (~3 weeks right after a restock) |
| shipped | shipping confirmation + tracking | — |
| in transit | tracking updates | 7-10 business days |
| scheduling | a call or email from the freight carrier | before delivery |

## why freight tracking looks stalled (and usually isn't)

a parcel scans at every depot, so you see steady movement. **freight moves in fewer, larger steps** — picked up, arrived at terminal, out for delivery — and a pallet can sit legitimately at a terminal overnight or over a weekend with no new scan.

**a day without an update is normal. two days across a weekend is normal.** it doesn't mean anything is lost. your **pro number** is the freight equivalent of a tracking number, and it can lag the physical shipment by up to a day — the pallet often moves before the scan catches up.

**accessories track normally** — cup holders, trays, mats, and organizers ship parcel with regular scans, so several days of silence on one of those is more meaningful than the same silence on a freight table.

## if the carrier hasn't reached out

for a table, the carrier (typically abf) contacts you directly to book the delivery appointment — check your voicemail, spam folder, and texts, since that call sometimes comes from an unfamiliar number. if tracking shows the shipment at a terminal near you and nobody has called within a couple of business days, that's worth flagging — see [freight delivery and scheduling](freight-delivery-and-scheduling.md).

## if it really has stalled

if several business days pass with no movement, the date on the product page has passed, a promised delivery window comes and goes with no call, or tracking says delivered and it isn't there — don't wait it out. contact us through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us) with your order number and we'll trace it with the carrier directly. tracing works better the earlier it starts — we'd rather know on day two than day ten.

d: The mat is meant to be a snug fit. If it reads as too long, adjust the rails to give the vault a little more room, then massage the slack out — never trim it.
h:
why my play mat doesn't fit the mat is meant to be a snug fit. if it reads as too long, adjust the rails to give the vault a little more room, then massage the slack out — never trim it. # why my play mat doesn't fit

**the mat is designed to be a snug fit in the play vault.** that's intentional — a snug mat sits flat and stays put instead of sliding around under a game.

so a mat that seems slightly too long usually isn't the wrong size. it's most often that the table sections aren't pulled fully together, which leaves the vault opening a fraction short of where it should be.

**don't trim it and don't force it.** this is nearly always fixable in a few minutes.

## adjust the rails, then settle the mat

**1. loosen the rail bolts.** underneath the table, loosen the bolts that fasten the rails to the table base.

**2. align the rails.** adjust their positioning to give a little more breathing room to the play vault, so the mat has room to sit.

**3. tighten.** once the rails are where you want them, fully tighten the bolts securing them.

**4. massage the mat into place.** set the ends of the mat into the corners so the slack lifts up as an air pocket. lightly press down on the air pockets and spread the slack out through the rest of the mat. it should settle and press against the rails — flat, and snug.

that last step is the one people skip, and it's usually what finishes the job. neoprene has some give; the slack doesn't need to be removed so much as distributed.

## if it still won't sit flat

**don't trim or modify it.** get in touch through our [claims form](https://zolamod.com/pages/claims-form) with your order number and a photo of how it's sitting, and our team will help diagnose it.

a photo settles this faster than a description — how the mat sits tells us more than how much it's over by.

## the sizes, for reference

the size in a pangea's name is the playable area — the recessed vault the mat sits in:

| table | vault |
|---|---|
| 3×3 | 36″ × 36″ |
| 3×5 | 36″ × 60″ |
| 4×6 | 48″ × 72″ |

the overall table is larger because the rails add about 3.25″ per side, but that's the outer footprint rather than the space a mat occupies. see [playable size vs. overall footprint](playable-size-vs-overall-footprint.md).

every pangea ships with a mat sized for its vault — see [play mats explained](play-mats-explained.md).

will it fit my room? measure against the overall footprint, not the playable size, and leave about 3 feet clear on every side you'll seat players. # will it fit my room?

two different measurements matter, and people usually check the wrong one first.

## measure the overall footprint, not the name

a pangea's name is its **playable area** — the recessed vault. the table itself is larger, because the rails add about 3.25″ per side.

| table | playable area | overall footprint |
|---|---|---|
| 3×3 | 36″ × 36″ | **42.5″ × 42.5″** |
| 3×5 | 36″ × 60″ | **42.5″ × 66.5″** |
| 4×6 | 48″ × 72″ | **54.5″ × 78.5″** |

height is 30.5″ with the standard legs, 26″ of clearance underneath.

## then add clearance for chairs

the footprint is the table. the room needs to hold the table *plus* people getting in and out of chairs.

**allow roughly 3 feet on every side you'll seat players.** that covers a pushed-back chair plus someone walking behind it. less than that and you'll be shuffling sideways past seated players all evening.

practically, for a 4×6 seating 8–10:

- table: 54.5″ × 78.5″ — about **4.5 ft × 6.5 ft**
- plus 3 ft each side: about **10.5 ft × 12.5 ft** of room

if you can't give three feet on all four sides, it still works — just seat players on the sides that have room, and put a short side against a wall.

## check the route in, separately

a room that fits the table is no use if the cartons can't reach it. the longest carton is roughly **47″ for a 3×3, 71″ for a 3×5, and 83″ for a 4×6**.

measure the narrowest point on the path: doorway, stair turn, elevator, hallway corner. and plan to **assemble it in the room it will live in** — once built, it won't fit back through a standard door.

## leg heights change the maths

three leg heights are available, and they suit different rooms:

- **standard (26″ clearance)** — dining-table height, the default.
- **counter (32″)** — taller, pairs with counter stools rather than dining chairs.
- **coffee (14″)** — low, for lounge seating.

our pangea mid-century dining chairs are made for the standard height. if you're going counter or coffee, plan seating separately.

## if you're between sizes

tell us the room dimensions, your usual player count, and the biggest game you play, through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us). sizing is easier to get right in a two-minute conversation than from a table of numbers.

h:
will my games fit? measure your biggest game's board plus player boards against the playable area — 36×36, 36×60, or 48×72 — rather than sizing by player count. # will my games fit?

the honest way to size a table is to measure the biggest thing you actually play, rather than starting from how many people are at it.

## the numbers to measure against

the playable area — the recessed vault — is what your game sits in:

| table | playable area |
|---|---|
| pangea 3×3 | 36″ × 36″ (91 × 91 cm) |
| pangea 3×5 | 36″ × 60″ (91 × 152 cm) |
| pangea 4×6 | 48″ × 72″ (122 × 183 cm) |

lay out your heaviest game on whatever you use now — main board, player boards, card rows, the tokens that spread — and measure the whole footprint. that number, not the box size, is what needs to fit.

## roughly what each size handles

- **3×3** — most mid-weight boxes comfortably. sized for dining nooks and compact rooms, seats 4.
- **3×5** — heavier games with player boards spread out and space that doesn't feel tight. seats 6.
- **4×6** — the big sprawls: twilight imperium, eclipse, large rpg maps, warhammer. seats 8–10, with room for each player's own area.

## two things people forget to include

**player boards spread outward.** a game whose main board is 24″ square can occupy twice that once four players have their own areas laid out. that's usually what pushes people from a 3×3 to a 3×5.

**the vault has depth.** 2.5″ of it. tall pieces, standing miniatures, and card holders sit *in* the recess rather than on a flat surface — so a game that feels cramped on a flat table often has more usable room here than the dimensions suggest.

## the room is the other half

a table that fits your game still has to fit the room, with clearance for chairs. that's the constraint that decides it more often than the game does — see [will it fit my room?](will-it-fit-my-room.md).

## if you're between two sizes

tell us the game, the group size, and the room, through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us). sizing is easier to get right in a short conversation than from a table of numbers, and we'd rather talk you into the right one than sell you the larger one.

- **doesn't fit the room** — a different leg height or reconfiguration sometimes solves it

## commercial use is covered

this is a change worth naming: commercial use used to void the warranty entirely. it doesn't any more. if you were told otherwise previously, this table is what's current.

## what counts as a defect

> an inadequacy in materials or workmanship that **existed at the time you received it**, and causes the product to fail under ordinary use, following the assembly and care instructions.

that test is what separates a covered defect from wear. within the periods above it covers structural defects, warping or cracking or separation of wooden components under normal use, and faulty hardware — leg mechanisms, magnets, rails, connectors, lift components.

**wear and defects can affect the same part.** a topper that arrives delaminating or warped is a defect. a topper worn down after two years of play is not — that's a consumable, and replacements are purchasable. see [wear versus a defect](wear-versus-a-defect.md).

## natural wood variation is not a defect

character marks, grain pattern, colour variation between panels and between production lots, and natural colour aging are inherent to real wood and veneer.

**cerused oak** in particular works pigment into open grain, so visible texture and tonal variation are the intended appearance rather than a fault. see [caring for your zola finish](caring-for-your-zola-finish.md).

## two things that are not warranty claims — and are faster anyway

**damage in transit.** freight damage sits outside the warranty and moves through a quicker path — but it must be reported **within 5 days of delivery**, with photos of the outer carton, the shipping label, and the damage. keep the packaging until you've checked everything; without those photos a carrier claim can't be filed. see [shipping damage vs. warranty claim](shipping-damage-vs-warranty-claim.md).

**a missing or broken part on arrival.** photo plus order number through our [contact page](https://zolamod.com/pages/contact-us). see [missing or broken replacement parts](missing-or-broken-replacement-parts.md).

the short version: **arrived damaged** → damage flow, 5-day window. **failed or defective in normal use** → warranty claim.
